children: ASTROTECH Corp reported fiscal 2026 revenue of $913K, down 13% from $1049K in FY 2025, and a net loss of $14.4M, slightly wider than the $13.9M loss in the prior year, according to its 10-K summary.
Revenue: $913K for FY 2026, down from $1,049K in FY 2025 (13.0%).
Net income: Net loss $14.4M for FY 2026, compared with net loss $13.9M for FY 2025 (loss widened by $0.6M).
Diluted EPS: Not provided in Part 2 Item 7 / Part 4 Item 15 and therefore omitted.
Product launches and commercialization: The company introduced the EN-SCAN line and Labrador HH-GC in 2025–2026, targeting rugged, field-portable GC/MS applications.
Revenue and channel momentum: TRACER 1000 deployments reached about 37 sites across 16 countries; while product sales declined year-over-year, consumables and training revenue increased.
Strategic realignment: The board approved Lunar Initiatives and is exploring a potential sale of 1st Detect to reallocate capital toward lunar and advanced computing opportunities.
Capital access and funding: ASTROTECH launched an ATM equity program and sold shares to support operations and scale commercialization efforts.
Regulatory and certification progress: The company began TSA Developmental Test & Evaluation for the TRACER 1000 to pursue checkpoint certification and broader security adoption.
This is an AI-powered summary. It may contain inaccuracies. Consider verifying important information with the source. Please note this summary is solely based on documents filed with the SEC.
